body.estimand_functional: \(\widehat\mu_c=\operatorname{clip}_{[-B,B]^T}\!\left\{\widehat U(\widehat U_{S_c}^{\prime}\widehat U_{S_c})^{-1}\widehat U_{S_c}^{\prime}\widehat\nu_c\right\},\qquad \mathcal R_N\lesssim\min\{1,(Ns_N^2)^{-1}\},\quad \mathcal W_{N,\alpha}\lesssim\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\},\quad \widehat\theta\text{ and }\widehat\rho_N\text{ defined by robust joint-moment blocks, with matching lower bounds conditional on legal same-shell deformation}\)

sampling_model.design: Observational short panel with deterministic cohort-specific untreated masks \(S_c\) and independent cross-sectional sampling.
sampling_model.treatment: For cohort \(c\), only \(J_cY_i(0)\) is used for recovery; observed treated outcomes may be appended and are held fixed in countermodels.
sampling_model.overlap: Every \(p_c\ge p_{\star}\) and every \(S_c\) has at least three coordinates; identification strength is \(s(P)\), not pairwise cohort overlap.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The joint cohort indicator, first-moment, and second-moment vector is estimated by coordinatewise median of means with a robust data-driven scale. Covariance PCA supplies point estimation. Honest inference profiles the distance to the compact primitive moment model and inverts a nonempty recentered \(\ell_\infty\) moment set.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their Theorem 1 establishes \(O_3\) acceptance as a sufficient mask condition for factor-plane identification.
Their Theorems 1 and 2 supply rank-two deterministic sampling count conditions for generic subspace identification and matrix completion.
Their Theorems 1--3 provide entrywise intervals and an instance-wise lower bound for a growing staggered-block matrix model.
Their weak-factor results derive minimax and honesty costs when factor strength or factor number is uncertain.
Their paper establishes uniformly valid identification-robust tests and confidence sets across weak, semi-strong, and strong sequences in broad extremum models.
Their Theorem 1 and corollaries give deterministic necessary and sufficient conditions for generic coordinate-subspace identifiability.
Their Theorem 1 bounds canonical-projection subspace error by projection noise divided by a relation singular value.
Their Theorems 10 and 12 identify generic entry completability with closure in the determinantal matroid through Jacobian row span.
Their Theorem 1.8 and pebble algorithms characterize and recognize sparse hypergraphs.

body.tldr: Short panels with systematic missing outcomes require gluing cohort-specific covariance eigenspaces before missing untreated means are causal functionals. A deterministic smallest-two anchor convention maps every mask to the published rank-two count certificate of Pimentel--Alarcón, Boston, and Nowak; Streinu--Theran pebble decision and extraction are background. The combinatorial contribution is limited to the causal consequence: complete-observed-law functionality and countermodels, together with the panel-specific corollary that Lei--Ross \(O_3\) acceptance implies count-certificate acceptance and masks \(123,145,256,346\) make the inclusion strict. Covariance PCA gives the squared-risk upper scale \(\min\{1,(Ns_N^2)^{-1}\}\). A coordinatewise robust joint-moment estimator, data-driven radius, and profile-recentered nonempty inversion rule give uniformly honest rectangles with upper half-width scale \(\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}\) and no asymptotic full-box fallback contribution. Matching lower frontiers remain conditional on the legal same-shell deformation obligation, whose four-mask slope path is the mandatory early-kill question.

project_justification.gap: Pimentel-Alarcón, Boston, and Nowak already provide the rank-two deterministic count criterion, and Streinu and Theran provide sparse-hypergraph pebble machinery. Lei and Ross provide \(O_3\)-sufficient identification and regular APM inference. What is absent is the causal transport from the published certificate to equality of complete observed panel laws, plus a mathematically total finite-moment inversion rule and a legal same-shell lower experiment for missing cohort means.
project_justification.niche: The unoccupied object is a fixed-\(T\) causal experiment with deterministic cohort masks, complete-observed-law countermodels when the published certificate fails, a strict panel-specific \(O_3\) containment witness, and uniformly honest simultaneous inference as the observable relation margin approaches zero.
project_justification.fill: The paper takes the published count and pebble results as inputs, proves their distinct full-law causal transport and countermodel consequence, and records \(O_3\) containment with the exact four-mask strict witness. It develops covariance-PCA risk bounds and profile-recentered inversion of a robust data-driven \(\ell_\infty\) joint-moment ball. Two-sided statistical frontiers are stated only conditional on legal same-shell deformations, with the four-mask path isolated as the early-kill obligation.

body.related_work: Pimentel-Alarcón, Boston, and Nowak provide the rank-two deterministic count criterion for generic subspace identification and matrix completion; that generic rank/count reduction is cited background rather than a novelty claim. Streinu and Theran supply the sparse-hypergraph pebble recognition, extraction, component algorithms, and complexity. Király, Theran, and Tomioka identify generic completion through Jacobian closure and determinantal matroids. The distinct combinatorial-to-causal step here preserves cohort-specific loading and error laws and either recovers every missing mean from the complete observed law or constructs two complete observed-law-equivalent causal panels. Lei and Ross provide the closest econometric setup: their \(O_3\) overlap-merging condition is sufficient for factor-plane identification and their APM estimator yields regular fixed-\(T\) inference. As a panel-specific corollary of the published count criterion, \(O_3\) acceptance implies canonical certificate acceptance, whereas masks \(123,145,256,346\) are certificate-accepted and \(O_3\)-rejected. Srivastava and Pimentel-Alarcón establish reciprocal-singular-value projection perturbation, leaving the legal same-shell causal lower experiment open. Yan and Wainwright inform the least-conditioned local experiment but study growing staggered-block matrices. Zhu informs weak-factor honesty costs, and Andrews and Cheng inform identification-robust inversion; neither specifies the robust joint-moment ball and profile-recentered panel inversion used here. Liu, Wang, and Xu provide a concrete consumer through the \(\operatorname{fect}\) counterfactual-imputation workflow.
body.technical_internal_limitation: At an observed law with all cohort means equal to zero, local rank forces every compatible missing mean to be zero even when the mask fails the published count certificate, so the converse is model-wide rather than pointwise at every observed law. Fully observed masks cannot generate a shrinking relation margin. Shell nonemptiness alone supplies no primitive interior slack and therefore licenses neither the minimax lower bound nor the honest-width lower bound. Those lower bounds and the necessity direction are conditional on the legal same-shell deformation property. The robust profile inversion is an exact mathematical optimization over a compact primitive closure; numerical certification is outside the theorem.
body.honest_scope: The smallest-two anchor convention is deterministic, and admissible loading means are the explicitly defined class \(\mathfrak M_{\lambda}(H)\). The rank-two count criterion and all generic pebble algorithms are published background. The proposal claims only their distinct complete-observed-law causal transport and countermodel consequence, plus the panel-specific corollary \(O_3\Rightarrow\) certificate acceptance and its strict four-mask witness. Covariance-PCA and the total profile-recentered robust moment inversion provide unconditional upper targets on nonempty shells. The latter uses the explicit \(\ell_\infty\) joint-moment norm, a coordinatewise median-of-means estimator, a data-driven scale, a finite-sample coverage lemma, and a fallback event that is empty for all sufficiently large \(N\). Matching risk and width lower bounds and necessity of \(Ns_N^2\to\infty\) remain conditional on the legal same-shell deformation result. The four-mask path is the early-kill obligation.
